title: India's GST Collections Hit 14-Month High, Cross Rs 2 Lakh Crore for Second Time in FY27
excerpt: July gross GST revenue surged past the Rs 2 lakh crore mark, driven by strong domestic consumption and rising import-linked tax collections.
body:
• Gross GST collections in July 2026 crossed Rs 2 lakh crore for the second time this fiscal year, reaching a 14-month high.
  • Import-linked GST revenue has been the standout contributor, with collections surging over 30% year-on-year in recent months.
  • Net GST revenue after refunds continues to grow in double digits, signaling sustained economic momentum.
  • The first quarter of FY27 (April-June) saw cumulative gross GST of Rs 6.32 lakh crore, up 8.4% over the prior year.

India's Goods and Services Tax collections in July 2026 crossed the Rs 2 lakh crore threshold for the second time this fiscal year, hitting a 14-month high and reinforcing the economy's strong growth trajectory.

Import Revenue Drives the Surge

The headline figure continues a pattern that has defined FY27's GST performance: import-linked tax collections are outpacing domestic revenue growth by a wide margin. In June 2026, the last month for which detailed breakdowns are available, gross import GST revenue jumped 34.6% year-on-year to Rs 60,038 crore, according to Finance Ministry data. Domestic GST grew a more modest 6.5% to Rs 1,34,774 crore.

The divergence reflects India's deepening integration into global trade networks, with imports of electronics, crude oil, and capital goods generating substantial tax revenue at ports and customs checkpoints.

FY27 Off to a Strong Start

For the April-June quarter of FY27, cumulative gross GST collections reached Rs 6,31,699 crore, an 8.4% increase over Rs 5,82,542 crore in the same period last year. Net collections — after accounting for refunds of Rs 32,436 crore in June alone — climbed 11.2% to Rs 1,62,377 crore.

"Monthly collections have crossed Rs 2 lakh crore for fourteen straight months — a 3x jump from the Rs 89,885 crore monthly average in GST's first year."

— Finance Ministry data analysis

State-Level Performance

Maharashtra maintained its position as the top GST-contributing state with collections of Rs 30,714 crore in June, followed by Karnataka and Gujarat — both recording double-digit growth. Uttar Pradesh stood out with a 19% increase, reflecting expanding economic activity in India's most populous state.

However, several states including Sikkim, Puducherry, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, and Tamil Nadu reported declines in collections during June, pointing to uneven recovery across regions.

What It Means for Investors

The sustained GST growth supports the government's fiscal consolidation path and suggests the Indian economy maintains solid consumer demand and business activity. For NRI investors tracking India's macro fundamentals, the expanding tax base — now covering over 1.51 crore registered taxpayers, up from 60 lakh at GST's 2017 launch — signals ongoing formalization of the economy.

Markets will watch whether the Rs 2 lakh crore monthly run rate holds through the monsoon quarter, which historically sees some softening in consumption patterns.
nri_angle: Strong GST data signals robust Indian economic fundamentals for NRI investors tracking macro indicators.
